Thank you for your review.
I have had the opportunity to listen to your and your brother's recorded telephone calls.  Firstly your brother contacted the Practice Manager via email complaining that he "had been kept on hold on the telephone for forty two minutes".  he sent a photograph from his mobile phone displaying that he had been waiting in a queue to be connected to the triage service. This photograph is not an indication that he had been kept on hold for forty two minutes. The Practice Manager telephoned him on the same day after listening to the two recordings from the number he stated he rang from.  One call was for 36 seconds and the other for 11 seconds where he connected to the Practice but did not speak therefore the call was disconnected. there were no other calls made to the Practice from that number since January 2024. 
He was advised that other patients are getting through  on the line it cannot be determined that there is a fault with the Practice telephone system.  He then stated "as I am complaining you should offer me something"?  He was advised to telephone the next day in triage. He was also advised that due to high demand there may be instances where Patients are waiting in a queue for longer than desired.  This is an issue within the NHS as a whole and not just pertaining to the Practice. The Practice Manager also advised that as there was no telephone call listed where he was left on hold she was not able to advise on any faults with the Practice telephone line.  If he had an issue the next time, to leave a message for her and she would ring him back after an investigation into the telephone system . He did not leave a message.  Pertaining to your issue you telephoned twice this morning.  Firstly you spoke with a receptionist stating "I have been on the phone for hours"?  It was 1010 and the telephone line operates from 0900.  You were advised that the triage lines had closed and to telephone at in the next triage session.  Meanwhile you were also advised to telephone NHS111 if you thought it necessary.  You proceeded to argue with the receptionist and amongst other statement you exclaimed "I am fasting - you lot clearly are not". Interestingly, they seem very communicative on reviews, unable to stop themselves from responding defensively because it's a public forum, yet they failed to return my call and hung up on me abruptly.
For reference, the GMC guidelines emphasise the importance of protecting patient information and maintaining confidentiality. Doctors have a duty to provide a good standard of practice and care, prioritising patient safety above all. But Surjit and Dr Ahmad admit they were covering themselves and were unable to explain how they had prioritised my mother's safety.
